title: Governance, Risk and Compliance for Market Infrastructures
summary: A ten-module programme for boards, managers and control functions of trading venues, CCPs, CSDs and payment systems on meeting the PFMI in governance, risk, default management and recovery.
intro: This training programme equips the boards, senior managers and control functions of trading venues, CCPs, CSDs and payment systems to meet the PFMI in practice: governing the infrastructure, managing financial and operational risk, handling defaults and planning for recovery.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give those who run and oversee market infrastructures a complete, practical view of what the PFMI and related standards require of them and how authorities test compliance. Participants leave able to strengthen governance and the risk framework, challenge models and stress tests, rehearse default management and recovery, and evidence resilience to their supervisors and overseers.
sections.What It Covers: The role and systemic importance of market infrastructures, the PFMI and the authorities' expectations, governance and ownership, the comprehensive risk framework, credit and liquidity risk, collateral, margin and procyclicality, default management, settlement finality and asset safekeeping, operational resilience and cyber, access, tiering, links and trading venue controls, and recovery, wind-down and supervisory engagement.
Intended Audience: Board members, risk and audit committee members and senior executives of trading venues, CCPs, CSDs, payment systems and trade repositories
Chief risk officers, heads of compliance, internal audit and risk, treasury, default management and operations staff
Regulatory affairs, legal and strategy teams preparing for supervisory assessments or new services
Learning Objectives: Explain the infrastructure's systemic role and how the PFMI frame what is expected of it
Evaluate governance, ownership and the comprehensive risk framework against the PFMI
Challenge credit, liquidity, margin and collateral models, stress tests and backtesting
Prepare and rehearse default management, recovery and orderly wind-down arrangements
Strengthen settlement, safekeeping, operational and cyber resilience and access arrangements
Evidence compliance and resilience to supervisors and overseers and agree an action plan
sections.Structure and Format: Ten modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a five-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a briefing with case studies, model challenge and fire drill exercises, and modules can be selected or tailored to the type of infrastructure and to board or practitioner audiences.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of trading, clearing, settlement or payment systems is helpful. No prior study of the PFMI is required.
Core Reading: CPMI-IOSCO, Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures (2012)
FSB, Key Attributes of Effective Resolution Regimes for Financial Institutions (2014)
IOSCO, Regulatory Issues Raised by Changes in Market Structure (2013)
FSB, Effective Practices for Cyber Incident Response and Recovery (2020)

modules.title: Market Infrastructures, Systemic Importance and the PFMI
modules.summary: What trading venues, CCPs, CSDs, payment systems and trade repositories do, why they both reduce and concentrate systemic risk, and how the PFMI and authorities' responsibilities shape what is expected of them.
objectives: Explain the functions and interdependencies of the main types of infrastructure
Identify why the firm's infrastructure is systemically important and what follows
Apply the structure of the PFMI, key considerations and disclosure framework
syllabus: The trade lifecycle from execution to clearing, settlement and reporting
Systemic importance, interdependencies and lessons from past disruptions
PFMI principles, key considerations and the assessment methodology
Supervision and oversight: what securities authorities and central banks expect

modules.title: Governance, Ownership and the Board
modules.summary: How ownership, board composition and committee structures shape decisions on risk, access and fees, and how the board balances commercial objectives with its public interest and risk management duties.
objectives: Assess board composition, independence and risk committee effectiveness
Manage conflicts between profitability, risk standards and open access
Design governance that gives participants and stakeholders a credible voice
syllabus: Ownership models: user-owned, listed groups and vertical silos
Board, risk committee and participant representation
Conflicts of interest, fees and commercial incentives
Transparency: disclosure framework and quantitative public disclosures

modules.title: The Comprehensive Risk Management Framework
modules.summary: How an infrastructure builds an integrated framework covering credit, liquidity, operational, business, custody and investment risk, and the role of the second and third lines in testing that it works.
objectives: Design an integrated risk framework, appetite and policies across all risk types
Organise the risk, compliance and internal audit functions for an infrastructure
Manage general business, custody and investment risk and the capital to cover them
syllabus: Risk appetite, policies and model governance
Independent risk, compliance and internal audit functions
General business risk, custody and investment risk
Model validation and independent review

modules.title: Credit and Liquidity Risk Management
modules.summary: How infrastructures measure and cover credit and liquidity exposures to participants, the cover standards and stress testing behind them, and how to defend model assumptions under supervisory challenge.
objectives: Measure current and potential future exposures to participants
Design stress testing, cover standards and qualifying liquid resources
Defend scenarios, model assumptions and backtesting results to the authority
syllabus: Current and potential future exposure; cover 1 and cover 2 standards
Liquidity needs, qualifying resources and settlement bank dependencies
Stress scenario design, reverse stress testing and backtesting
Weaknesses supervisors look for: optimistic scenarios, wrong-way risk and stale models

modules.title: Collateral, Margin and Procyclicality
modules.summary: How initial and variation margin and collateral policies protect the infrastructure, the trade-off between prudence and procyclicality, and how to calibrate and communicate margin to participants.
objectives: Calibrate initial margin models, look-back periods and confidence levels
Set eligible collateral, haircuts and concentration limits
Manage procyclicality and the transparency of margin calls in stress
syllabus: Initial and variation margin: purpose, methods and calibration
Collateral eligibility, haircuts, concentration limits and reuse
Anti-procyclicality tools and margin transparency for participants
Lessons from margin spikes in commodity and bond market stress

modules.title: Default Management and Fire Drills
modules.summary: How the infrastructure prepares for and handles a participant default, from declaration, close-out and auction to the default waterfall, and how fire drills test that procedures work under pressure.
objectives: Design default rules, procedures and the sequence of the default waterfall
Size the default fund and the infrastructure's own resources at risk
Plan and run default management fire drills and auctions
syllabus: Declaring a default, porting client positions and close-out
Default waterfall: margin, default fund, own resources and assessments
Auction design, participant obligations and hedging
Fire drill design, findings and remediation

modules.title: Settlement, Finality and Asset Safekeeping
modules.summary: How settlement finality, money settlement, delivery versus payment and CSD safekeeping remove principal and custody risk, including the questions raised by DLT-based and tokenised settlement.
objectives: Establish the legal basis and moment of settlement finality
Manage DvP and PvP models, money settlement assets and settlement bank risk
Protect participants' assets through account structures and reconciliation
syllabus: Legal certainty and the moment of finality
DvP, PvP and central bank versus commercial bank money
Settlement fails, buy-ins and integrity of the issue
DLT settlement, tokenised assets and stablecoin arrangements under the PFMI

modules.title: Operational Resilience, Cyber and Critical Service Providers
modules.summary: How infrastructures manage operational, cyber and third-party risk, meet the expectation of rapid recovery and evidence resilience against severe but plausible scenarios.
objectives: Design operational risk and business continuity arrangements to recovery objectives
Strengthen cyber resilience, including recovery from data corruption
Manage dependencies on critical service providers and cloud
syllabus: Two-hour recovery objective and severe but plausible scenarios
CPMI-IOSCO cyber resilience guidance, threat-led testing and data integrity
Critical service providers, cloud concentration and exit options
Incident management, root cause analysis and notification

modules.title: Access, Tiering, Links and Trading Venue Controls
modules.summary: How to set fair, risk-based access criteria, manage the risks of tiered participation, client clearing and links, and operate the trading controls and surveillance expected of a venue.
objectives: Set risk-based, fair and open participation requirements and exit procedures
Manage risks from indirect participants, client clearing and links
Operate trading venue controls that support orderly markets
syllabus: Access criteria, monitoring and suspension of participants
Tiered participation, client segregation and portability
CCP links, CSD links and interoperability exposures
Trading venue rules, circuit breakers and market surveillance

modules.title: Recovery, Wind-Down and Supervisory Engagement
modules.summary: Brings the programme together: recovery planning and loss allocation, orderly wind-down and resolution, preparing for supervisory assessment and cooperative oversight, and a workshop on an infrastructure under stress.
objectives: Design recovery plans, triggers and tools for uncovered losses and liquidity shortfalls
Prepare orderly wind-down plans and support resolution planning
Evidence PFMI compliance to supervisors and overseers in assessments and crises
syllabus: Recovery tools: cash calls, variation margin gains haircutting and tear-ups
Orderly wind-down, liquid net assets and the Key Attributes
Self-assessments, cooperative oversight and crisis management groups
Workshop: a participant default with cross-border spillovers

related.title: Crypto-Asset Compliance Programme
related.summary: An advanced twelve-module programme for compliance, risk and MLRO staff at crypto-asset service providers, from authorisation and custody to market abuse, AML/CFT and wind-down.

related.title: Fund Governance and Compliance for Managers and Service Providers
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving fund managers and service providers the practical tools to meet fund rules and supervisory expectations across the fund lifecycle.

related.title: Investment Services Compliance
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving compliance and risk staff at investment firms the tools to build, test and evidence compliance across the client journey and market activity.

related.title: Payments and E-Money Compliance
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving payment and e-money firms the practical tools to meet safeguarding, fraud, financial crime and resilience expectations.

related.title: Private Markets and Private Credit for Managers
related.summary: An eight-module advanced programme giving private markets managers and service providers the tools to manage valuation, leverage, liquidity and conflicts risks and meet supervisory expectations.

related.title: Embedded Finance, Open Finance and Big Tech Partnerships
related.summary: A nine-module programme for firms building embedded finance, open finance and platform partnerships, covering partnership models, responsibility, partner oversight, data sharing, customer outcomes and exit.
